item.text:
**Verdict**
- `7B.2`: mixed, leaning no. I found one limited transparency case on Trọng’s health handoff, but the stronger 2024 pattern is concealment, denial, and punishment of critics/truth-tellers rather than routine admission of error or correction of false claims.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Politburo issues notice on Party General Secretary's health** | Government of Viet Nam | 2024-07-18 | [URL](https://en.baochinhphu.vn/politburo-issues-notice-on-party-general-secretarys-health-111240718161208612.htm)  
  The party officially disclosed that Trọng had been working while receiving treatment and transferred authority to Tô Lâm. This is the clearest evidence of disclosure, but it was late and reactive rather than a pattern of candid self-correction.  
  `Question IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1`

- **Vietnam: Free Prominent Journalist** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-06-07 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/07/vietnam-free-prominent-journalist)  
  HRW says Huy Duc was detained under an overly broad speech law, his family was not informed for seven days, and he could not meet lawyer or family. That supports a finding that truthful reporting was penalized, not protected.  
  `Question IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1`

- **Vietnam: New Wave of Arrests of Critics** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-05 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/05/vietnam-new-wave-arrests-critics)  
  HRW reports arrests of critics and quotes police framing dissident posts as content that “bend the truth” and smear leaders. This is strong evidence of state truth-control and intimidation of people exposing inconvenient facts.  
  `Question IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1`

- **Vietnam arrests two well-known Facebook users over democratic freedom abuse** | Reuters via Yahoo | 2024-06-08 | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/vietnam-arrests-two-well-known-034901151.html)  
  Reuters reported the arrests of journalist Truong Huy San and lawyer Tran Dinh Trien after critical Facebook posts, with home searches and investigations. This supports the view that the regime punished public criticism rather than tolerating correction of official narratives.  
  `Question IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1`

- **Rights group accuses Vietnam misleading US on human trafficking** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-20 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/rights-group-accuses-vietnam-misleading-us-on-human-trafficking-3490556)  
  Reuters reported accusations that Vietnam told officials to withhold information and present anti-trafficking efforts in a better light for U.S. reporting. This is direct evidence of deliberate misleading behavior in a reputation-sensitive domain.  
  `Question IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1`

- **Việt Nam expresses regrets over US human rights report** | Vietnam News | 2024-04-25 | [URL](https://vietnamnews.vn/politics-laws/1654576/viet-nam-expresses-regrets-over-us-human-rights-report.html)  
  The foreign ministry rejected the U.S. report as based on false information and biased comments. This is not an admission of error; it is a denial posture that fits the broader pattern of deflecting criticism rather than correcting the record.  
  `Question IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1`

- **3 chủ tài khoản Facebook bị phạt vì xuyên tạc Tổng bí thư Nguyễn Phú Trọng** | VnExpress | 2024-07-22 | [URL](https://vnexpress.net/3-chu-tai-khoan-facebook-bi-phat-vi-xuyen-tac-tong-bi-thu-nguyen-phu-trong-4772804.html)  
  Vietnamese authorities fined or summoned Facebook users for allegedly distorting Trọng’s death and reputation. This shows active punishment of people who challenge the leadership’s preferred narrative.  
  `Question IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1`

- **Freedom on the Net 2024: Vietnam** | Freedom House | 2024 | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/vietnam/freedom-net/2024)  
  Freedom House notes that when Trọng disappeared from public view in early 2024, mainstream Vietnamese media did not report his absence; foreign media broke the story instead. That is weak positive evidence on “allowing” reporting only in the sense that the internet was not fully shut down, but self-censorship and selective silence remained strong.  
  `Question IDs: 7B.2`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Trọng personally admitted a substantive error, corrected a false public claim, or openly reversed a misleading statement.
- The strongest available evidence goes the other way: delayed health disclosure, official denial of criticism, and punishment of journalists or online critics.
